Anecdotally, my boss was like," hey design a 12 by 8 shed for me that I can build as cheap as possible, using only whats in stock at home depot", no problem. Next day, "it's for chickens can you add some insulation?" Sure can but that's a vastly different request.

You need to insulate your floor, walls and roof. You are going to have a HECK of a time trying to insulate underneath her now. I would probably use styrofoam at this point because I doubt you will be able to get enough clearance to keep anything else from getting wet. After you insulate her from the bottom (or perhaps you can pull up that subfloor and make it easier) I'd gets some rocks, patio stones, cinder blocks, whatever is cheap and available, and put them underneath your joists along the bottom, almost brick it off if you will.

Two reasons: much better foundation now, and second, it keeps the wind and snow out, boosting your insulation.

Remember that's a small volume with a lot of surface area, it's going to need a lot of insulation. And thats not cheap. The most water resistant is styrofoam and it's got a decent rR rating. Styrofoam is free if you can get a good source (raiding recycling bins is one way). To join the rag tag pieces together get the real cheap stray foam insulation (not the cans, I mean the big containers) and spray it in like a glue and around all your joists. The second advantage is if you have holes or cracks that spray foam will fill them all up.

I would put in a drop ceiling and give yourself at least 8 inches of insulation on the top (will help with the noise from the sheet roof too).

Lastly you need to sheathe it from inside. Walls, floor and ceiling with plastic 8 mil or 6 mil or whatever you need in that zone. Thats two part as well: it's your last defense against drafts and it keep moisture from you and whatever else you are doing in there from trying to go outside and condensing on colder wood. Then you get moisture in your walls, rot, mold, frost, ice, bobs your uncle.
